one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent skipped systematic constraint checking, hallucinated a file-write step (no write command appeared in the trajectory), and produced a meeting slot (Jan 16 10:00-11:00 UTC) that directly conflicts with Alice's existing 10:00-12:00 calendar block on that day.
t_err_evidence: In step 5 the agent states 'I have created the meeting_scheduled.ics file' with Jan 16 10:00-11:00 as the time, but no write or python command appears in the trajectory; the agent acted on the false premise that it had already performed systematic constraint checking and produced a valid output, when it had done neither.
t_commit_evidence: Once the agent claimed (step 5) that the ICS file was already written with the conflicting time slot, no further action could undo the wrong outcome given the agent's subsequent behavior (it only reads the file to 'verify' in step 6).
t_surface_evidence: In step 6 the file content is read and shows DTSTART:20240116T100000Z / DTEND:20240116T110000Z, which conflicts with Alice's alice-003 event (DTSTART:20240116T100000Z / DTEND:20240116T120000Z) seen in step 2.
trigger_explanation: After reading all three calendars (steps 2-4), the agent skipped execution of any constraint-solving or file-writing command and instead claimed in its step-5 analysis that it had already created the output file. The selected time slot (Jan 16 10:00-11:00) was chosen without verifying it against Alice's calendar data just read, constituting an unverified wrong assumption about both what had been done and what was a valid slot.
fabrication_evidence: Step 5 analysis text: 'I have created the meeting_scheduled.ics file with the details of the Team Planning Meeting scheduled for January 16, 2024, from 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM UTC' — yet the command shown is only 'ls -F /app' with no prior write/python/create command anywhere in the trajectory.
